description.narrative:
Stakeholder Effect: Increased access to finance for SMEs: IFC anticipates that the proposed investment will help increase access to finance for SMEs in India, especially those in the technology sector. Alteria will leverage its expertise and know-how of providing financing to these high growth SMEs through secured debt products under the fund. By expanding the types of funding especially shorter-term funding that venture debt managers can provide to tech SMEs, the Project will contribute to increased access to finance for the fast-growing start-up sector in India. The tech SMEs that ACF3 SDS will support are mostly digital financial services companies and consumer products and services companies that will turn help increase access to finance in India.
Market Creation: Competitiveness: IFC anticipates that via innovation, demonstration and replication channels, the Project will promote greater competitiveness within the SME financing sector by increasing financing available to SMEs especially those are technology driven. The proposed fund represents the first strategy in the market to specifically address the gap of shorter-term financing to tech-SMEs offered by a debt fund, as a distinct segment through Shorter Duration Scheme (SDS).

The proposed project envisages an investment of up to US$12 million in INR equivalent in a target US$100 million Alteria Capital Fund III Shorter Duration Scheme (ACF3 SDS or the Fund) debt fund, managed by Alteria Venture Partners LLP (AVP or Alteria or Fund Manager). The Fund will provide short-term secured debt to venture capital backed start-ups (the Project). The companies will be digital finance services (DFS) providers as well as will include consumer products, B2B platforms, Climate tech and services companies in India. These companies will be technology driven micro, medium and small enterprises (MSMEs).
